title: Last-Coverage Probabilities of Random Walks on Cycle Graphs for Symmetric, Biased, and Time-Dependent Walks
summary: This paper studies the last-coverage vertex of a nearest-neighbour random walk on a cycle: the vertex most likely to be the final one discovered. We show that the visited vertices always form a single contiguous arc of the ring, a property we call the Connected Arc Property. This lets the walk be replaced by a two-state time-inhomogeneous Markov chain, which we call the interval-expansion representation, in which each expansion step has a probability given by the classical gambler's ruin formula.
